units: Gen. R. s. 16 פ׳ שפ̇ר̇ה ורבה וכ׳ it is named P’rath (the growing), for its waters grow and increase, until people pass it on ships; פ׳ שמימיו פרין ורבין וכ׳ P’rath, for its waters are fruitful (fructifying); פ׳ שמפ̇ר̇יד והולך עד שכלה במגריפה ‘Rashi’ (ed. שמפרש) it is named P’rath (v. פְּרַת), because it goes on dividing (branching off in channels), until it ends under the (digging) spade; Yalk. Deut. 801 כמגרפה (corr. acc.); Sifré Deut. 6 שמפרה והולך עד שכלה מגריפה לגרפי it goes on fructifying (irrigating), until the spade ceases to dig it; Yalk. Gen. 22 מפריס והולך עד שהוא כלה ופותחין וכ׳ goes on dividing, until it disappears, and they open it with the spade.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 137:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. CXXXVII</cite> <he>שתו מים הפ׳ ומתים</he> they drank Euphrates water and died; (<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 28:1">Pesik. R. s. 28</cite> <he>מימי הפרת</he>).

senses.gloss: P’rath, name of certain districts or towns.

X, 11</cite>): <he>פ׳ דבורסיף</he> (= <he>כלח</he> <cite ref="Genesis 10:11">ib.</cite>); <cite ref="Kiddushin 72a:3">Kidd. 72ᵃ</cite> (expl. <he>חביל ימא</he>) <he>פ׳ דבורסי</he>, v. <cite ref="B00386"><he>בּוֹרְסִיף</he></cite>.
